extracted.intended_audience: individuals seeking access/correction of USPTO records and USPTO Privacy Officer/USPTO staff implementing the Privacy Act procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and substantive criteria for individuals to request, access, correct/amend, and obtain disclosure of USPTO records under the Privacy Act, and for USPTO staff (Privacy Officer, General Counsel) to process, respond, and adjudicate such requests and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information required in an inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: If the inquiry is a request that USPTO determine whether it has, in a given system of records, a record which pertains to the individual, the following information should be submitted:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: (1) Name of individual whose record is sought; (2) Individual is either a U.S. citizen or an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence; (3) Identifying data to help locate the record (e.g., maiden name, occupational license number, period/place of employment); (4) Record sought, by description and by record system name, if known; (5) Action requested (e.g., send info on rights under the Act; determine whether record exists; gain access; obtain copy); (6) Copy of court guardianship order or minor's birth certificate if requester is guardian/parent (§102.24(f)(3)); (7) Requester's name (printed), signature, address, telephone number (optional); (8) Date; (9) Certification of request by notary or other official, but only if (i) request is for notification that requested record exists, for access, or for copy; (ii) record is not available to any person under 5 U.S.C. 552; and (iii) requester does not appear before a USPTO employee for verification of identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing and marking mailed requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests submitted by mail should include the words 'PRIVACY ACT REQUEST' in capital letters at the top of the letter and on the face of the envelope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any request not properly addressed or marked will be so addressed and marked by USPTO personnel and forwarded to the Privacy Officer; a misaddressed request is not deemed 'received' for timeliness until actually received by the Privacy Officer. The Privacy Officer must notify the sender that the request was improperly addressed and the date it was received at the proper address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response timing and acknowledgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inquiry/request received shall be acted upon promptly by the Privacy Officer; every effort will be made to respond within ten working days of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a response cannot be made within ten working days, the Privacy Officer shall send an acknowledgment during that period providing status and asking for further information if necessary. The first correspondence must contain the USPTO control number assigned to the request and note that the requester should use that number in all future contacts. If the Privacy Officer fails to send an acknowledgment within ten working days, the requester may ask the General Counsel to take corrective action; such a failure does not confer administrative finality for judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to state a reason for inquiry or request
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual shall not be required to state a reason or otherwise justify his or her inquiry or request for access to a record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity verification — in person (acceptable proofs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual making a request in person shall be required to present satisfactory proof of identity. The means of proof, in the order of preference and priority, are:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (i) A document bearing the individual's photograph (e.g., driver's license, passport, military/civilian ID); (ii) A document bearing the individual's signature, preferably issued for participation in a federally sponsored program (e.g., unemployment insurance book, employer ID card, national credit card, professional/union membership card); (iii) A document bearing neither photo nor signature, preferably issued for participation in a federally sponsored program (e.g., Medicaid card). If no suitable documentation can be provided, USPTO will require a signed statement asserting identity and acknowledging penalty provisions (5 U.S.C. 552a(i)(3)). USPTO reserves the right to determine adequacy of proof of identity, particularly for sensitive records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity verification — not in person (notary certification)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the individual does not appear in person, a certification of a notary public or equivalent officer empowered to administer oaths must accompany the request under prescribed circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certification must be substantially in accordance with the provided text (City/County statement affirming the individual's signature, identity to the notary's satisfaction, commission expiration, signature). Also applies where §102.23(b)(9) requires certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parents and legal guardians — additional proof and representation limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual acting as the parent of a minor or the legal guardian of the individual to whom a record pertains must establish personal identity and identity in the representative capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For parents of minors, proof is certified or authenticated copy of the minor's birth certificate. For legal guardians, proof is certified or authenticated copy of the court's order declaring incapacity. A parent or guardian may represent only a living individual (not a decedent). A parent or guardian may be accompanied during personal access subject to §102.25(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant of access — notification contents
rubrics_metrics.description: When access is granted, the Privacy Officer will notify the individual and provide specific information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification will include: (i) Methods of access available; (ii) Place at which the record may be inspected; (iii) Earliest date the record may be inspected and the period it will remain available (earliest date no later than 30 calendar days from notification); (iv) Estimated date by which a copy could be mailed and estimate of fees under §102.31 (estimated date no later than 30 calendar days from notification); (v) Fact that the individual may be accompanied by another individual during personal access, subject to §102.25(f); (vi) Any additional requirements needed to grant access to a specific record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of access to records
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods of access that may be available depending on circumstances include inspection in person, transfer to a more convenient federal facility, and copies mailed at the individual's request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspection may be in a location specified by the Privacy Officer during business hours. Transfer to another Federal facility may be arranged only if the Privacy Officer determines a suitable facility is available, the access can be properly supervised there, and transmittal will not unduly interfere with USPTO operations or involve unreasonable costs. Copies may be mailed subject to payment of fees (§102.31); USPTO may elect to mail a copy on its own initiative at no charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on access to originals
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO reserves the right to limit access to copies and abstracts of original records rather than the originals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This election is appropriate when records are in automated data media (tape/diskette), when the record contains information on other individuals, or when deletion of information is permissible under exemptions (e.g., 5 U.S.C. 552a(k)(2)). Original records will not be made available except under the immediate supervision of the Privacy Officer or designee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accompaniment by another individual during personal access
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual requesting access may be accompanied by another individual of his or her choice; 'accompanied' includes discussion of the record in the presence of the other individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The individual to whom the record pertains shall authorize the presence of the other individual in writing. The authorization shall include the name of the other individual, a specific description of the record sought, the USPTO control number, the date, and signature of the individual to whom the record pertains. The other individual shall sign the authorization in the presence of the Privacy Officer. An individual shall not be required to state a reason for being accompanied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for initial denial of access
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to a record pertaining to an individual will be denied only upon a determination by the Privacy Officer that specific grounds apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds include: (i) The record is exempt under §102.33 or §102.34, or exempt by determination of another agency publishing notice of the system of records; (ii) The record is information compiled in reasonable anticipation of a civil action or proceeding; (iii) Provisions of §102.26 pertaining to medical records temporarily invoked; (iv) The individual has unreasonably failed to comply with the procedural requirements of this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for denial notices
rubrics_metrics.description: When access is denied, the Privacy Officer shall give notice in writing and include specified information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must include: (i) Privacy Officer's name and title/position; (ii) Date of the denial; (iii) Reasons for the denial, including citation to the appropriate section of the Act and this part; (iv) The individual's opportunities, if any, for further administrative consideration, including identity and address of responsible official, or statement that the denial is administratively final; (v) If administratively final within USPTO, the individual's right to judicial review under 5 U.S.C. 552a(g)(1) as limited by 5 U.S.C. 552a(g)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative review of initial denials and exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for further administrative consideration vary depending on the basis for denial (exemption, anticipation of litigation, procedural failures, medical records).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For denials under exemptions, two alternative opportunities: (A) contest application of the exemption (review procedures in §102.25(g)(3)(ii)); or (B) challenge the exemption itself via petition for issuance/amendment/repeal of a rule under 5 U.S.C. 553(e) filed with the General Counsel. Denials under other grounds may be reviewed by filing for review with the General Counsel and following §102.28 procedures to the maximum extent practicable. Denials under medical-record temporary invocation are not administratively final until expiration of the time period in §102.26(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special procedures for medical records
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical records have additional protective procedures before disclosure or access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No response to any request for access to medical records will be issued for seven working days from receipt. USPTO uses a routine use to consult an individual's physician/psychologist if, in USPTO's sole judgment, disclosure could have an adverse effect. In every case, the Privacy Officer shall: (1) inform of the waiting period; (2) obtain name/address of physician/psychologist if individual consents; (3) obtain specific written consent to consult physician/psychologist if advisable; (4) obtain specific written consent to provide medical records to physician/psychologist if access is best effected under guidance; (5) forward the medical record to USPTO's medical expert for review and determination whether consultation/transmittal is warranted. If consultation/transmittal occurs, the medical expert shall so act and provide instruction to the Privacy Officer regarding conditions of access. If the individual refuses to give names/consents and USPTO has determined disclosure could have adverse effect, USPTO shall give access by means of a copy sent registered mail return receipt requested at no cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for requests for correction or amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for correction or amendment should include specific information identifying the record, the proposed changes, and the basis for the requested correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: (1) Specific identification of the record sought to be corrected/amended (description, title, date, paragraph, sentence, line, words); (2) Specific wording to be deleted, if any; (3) Specific wording to be inserted/added, if any, and exact place; (4) Statement of basis for the requested correction/amendment with all available supporting documents/materials substantiating the statement. The statement should identify the criterion of the Act being invoked (whether information is unnecessary, inaccurate, irrelevant, untimely or incomplete). Mail requests should be marked 'PRIVACY ACT REQUEST'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review timing and disposition of correction/amendment requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The Privacy Officer shall acknowledge receipt of a correction/amendment request and either make the correction or deny the request within defined timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not later than ten working days after receipt, send an acknowledgment providing an estimate of time for action and asking for further information if necessary. No acknowledgment if review and notification can be completed within ten working days. 'Promptly' means within thirty working days; if the Privacy Officer cannot determine within thirty working days, the individual will be advised of the reason and an estimated decision date. Prompt actions: (i) make the correction/amendment and advise the individual in writing, providing copy of corrected/amended record or a statement of means whereby correction was effected; or (ii) inform the individual in writing that the request is denied and provide name/title, date, reasons with citation to Act/subpart, and procedures for appeal (§102.29).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for reviewing requests for correction or amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Privacy Officer will consider a set of criteria when reviewing a request for correction or amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria to be considered: (1) Sufficiency of the evidence submitted by the individual; (2) Factual accuracy of the information; (3) Relevance and necessity of the information in terms of purpose for which it was collected; (4) Timeliness and currency of the information in light of the purpose; (5) Completeness of the information in terms of the purpose; (6) Degree of risk that denial could unfairly result in determinations adverse to the individual; (7) Character of the record sought to be corrected or amended; (8) Propriety and feasibility of complying with the specific means of correction or amendment requested by the individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for denial of correction or amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction or amendment of a record requested by an individual will be denied only upon certain determinations by the Privacy Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial grounds include: (1) Individual failed to establish, by a preponderance of the evidence, the propriety of correction/amendment in light of §102.28(c) criteria; (2) Record sought to be corrected/amended is part of the official record in a terminated judicial/quasi-judicial/quasi-legislative proceeding to which the individual was a party/participant; (3) The information or record is subject of a pending judicial/quasi-judicial/quasi-legislative proceeding to which the individual is a party/participant; (4) The correction/amendment would violate a duly enacted statute or promulgated regulation; (5) The individual has unreasonably failed to comply with procedural requirements of this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to notify prior recipients after correction/amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever an individual's record is corrected or amended pursuant to a request, the Privacy Officer must notify all persons and agencies to which the corrected/amended portion had been disclosed prior to correction/amendment, if an accounting of such disclosure was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification shall require the recipient agency maintaining the record to acknowledge receipt of the notification, to correct or amend the record, and to apprise any agency or person to which it had disclosed the record of the substance of the correction or amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal procedures and timelines for denied correction/amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: When an initial denial of correction/amendment occurs, the individual may submit a written appeal and follow specified procedures and timelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal must be filed within thirty working days after the date of initial denial (postmark conclusive). Address appeal to General Counsel and mark 'PRIVACY APPEAL' on letter and envelope. Appeal must include statement of reasons why initial denial is in error and provide USPTO control number and signature. No personal appearance or hearing on appeal. General Counsel shall issue a final determination in writing not later than thirty working days from receipt (may extend with written notice; estimate should not be later than 60 working days absent unusual circumstances). If appeal is granted, final determination will include specific corrections/amendments and copies transmitted to the individual and Privacy Officer; Privacy Officer must promptly take actions in §102.28(a)(2)(i) and (b). If denied, the notice shall inform the individual of the right to file a concise (ordinarily one-page) statement of disagreement, how it will be handled/appended/disclosed, and the right to judicial review under 5 U.S.C. 552a(g)(1)(A) as limited by 5 U.S.C. 552a(g)(5). The General Counsel shall employ the criteria in §102.28(c) and may deny an appeal only on grounds in §102.28(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of records to persons other than the individual — permissible instances
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO may disclose a record pertaining to an individual to a person other than the individual only in specified instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible instances include: (a)(1) upon written request by the individual, including authorization under §102.25(f); (a)(2) with the prior written consent of the individual; (a)(3) to a parent or legal guardian under 5 U.S.C. 552a(h); (a)(4) when required by the Act and not covered explicitly by 5 U.S.C. 552a(b); (a)(5) when permitted under 5 U.S.C. 552a(b)(1) through (12). Examples under (a)(5) include disclosures to agency employees with a need-to-know; required under 5 U.S.C. 552; routine uses as defined; to Bureau of the Census; to recipients giving assurances for statistical research in non-identifiable form; to National Archives; to another agency for law enforcement activity with written request; to persons in compelling health/safety circumstances (with notice to last known address); to Congress or its committees; to the Comptroller General; pursuant to court order; or to consumer reporting agencies under 31 U.S.C. 3711(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory situations requiring or authorizing disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain provisions of 5 U.S.C. 552a require or authorize disclosure in specific circumstances which are incorporated into USPTO practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situations referred to include: dissemination of corrected/amended records or notation of a disagreement statement under 5 U.S.C. 552a(c)(4); disclosure to the individual under 5 U.S.C. 552a(d); authorization of civil action and disclosure to courts under 5 U.S.C. 552a(g). (Note: 5 U.S.C. 552a(b)(4) has no application within USPTO.)
